plain_english: Never proved by non-spreading — though joined with knowing and the rest — breath and kin would be knowables, never knowers. Otherwise, delusion.
sanskrit_cite: na siddho 'prathanād eva jñānādisamavāyy api tat prāṇādi prameyaṃ syān na pramātānyato bhramāt

plain_english: Though the abiding of things stands locked in the living, curbed by breath and the eightfold city — even there, in the supreme self it abides.
sanskrit_cite: yady apy arthasthitiḥ prāṇapuryaṣṭakaniyantrite jīve niruddhā tatrāpi paramātmani sā sthitā

plain_english: How could restraint by breath of that self-nature ever be proved — in recognition? By living-ness, beyond non-showing.
sanskrit_cite: tadātmanaiva tasya syāt kathaṃ prāṇena yantraṇā sādhitā pratyabhijñāyām akhyāter jīvatā param

plain_english: No ordering of things lies in breath and the rest through blocking of I-ness; shining's self-rest is sung as I-ness, indeed.
sanskrit_cite: nārthavyavasthā prāṇādāv ahaṃbhāvanirodhataḥ prakāśasyātmaviśrāntir ahaṃbhāvo hi kīrtitaḥ

plain_english: Told already — that very rest, by blocking of all dependence: freedom, then doership foremost, and lordship too.
sanskrit_cite: uktā saiva ca viśrāntiḥ sarvāpekṣānirodhataḥ svātantryam atha kartṛtvaṃ mukhyam īśvaratāpi ca

plain_english: Called Māyā, of his power alone — with no other proven; this world-maker lordship is made of non-showing.
sanskrit_cite: māyābhidās tacchakter eva cānyāprasiddhitaḥ tadakhyātimayaṃ hy etaj jagannirmātṛteśitā

plain_english: One alone through linking, proclaimed: of all awarenesses the mother-principle, self-feeling's synonym — beginningless.
sanskrit_cite: ekaiva cānusaṃdhānāt sā proktā sarvasaṃvidām svasaṃvedanaparyāyamātṛtattvam anādi tat

plain_english: Whatever grounds the ordering of things — pervasion and linking of the I-sharer — fits nothing inert.
sanskrit_cite: bhāvavyavasthā yan niṣṭhā tasyāhaṃbhāvabhāginaḥ vyāpitvam anusaṃdhānaṃ taj jaḍasya na yujyate

plain_english: So within difference, shining's shining holds good — hence recognition's word: this world is that-nondual-made.
sanskrit_cite: tato bhede tu bhāsasya ghaṭate bhāsamānatā tenoktam pratyabhijñāyāṃ tadadvayamayaṃ jagat
